_README: Fields of NativeTrackSnapshot the browser deliberately does NOT carry, each with a reason.
This file is the second half of check-abi-coverage.mjs, and it is what lets the check be strict:
every engine field must be either CARRIED end-to-end or listed here. There is no third state — so
'nobody noticed', which is exactly how P8-10(a) happened (the ABI carried 12 of 125 fields and the
browser played a different piece of audio), stops being possible.
Add a field to NativeTrackSnapshot and the check FAILS until you either wire it through (5 steps,
which it prints) or put it here and say why. Both are fine answers. Silence is not.
AN ENTRY HERE IS A REAL GAP IN THE BROWSER, not a shrug. A session using one of these plays
WITHOUT it in the companion. It is still preserved in the file — PatternFile round-trips it
untouched (preserve-don't-drop), so nothing is LOST; it just does not SOUND. Keep this list short.

notCarried.trackType: MIDI/instrument. P8-9: a browser cannot host an AU/VST3, so instrument tracks are inert-but-preserved BY DESIGN, not by omission.
notCarried.midiChannel: MIDI hardware. The WASM build sets SCOOPY_MIDI_HARDWARE=0 — the engine's MIDI-out is compiled out entirely.
notCarried.instrumentOutEnabled: Instrument hosting. P8-9 — explicitly out of scope for the companion.
notCarried.launchAnchorStep: Transient launch scheduling, not document state. The engine sets it when a clip is launched; a session does not persist it and the companion has no launch surface.
notCarried.grainEnabled: Runtime gate, not document state. The document stores grainModeEnabled — which IS carried; grainEnabled is the engine's own armed flag.
notCarried.tpMorphEligible: Rate Morph v1 runtime gate (T+P × REG, resolved by the desktop facade). The browser applies detent changes instantly — rateMorphFrames defaults to 0 there, so the flag is inert. Nothing is lost: the document stores speedMode, which PatternFile round-trips.
